input:
Basis
This report presents the design of a distillation column that separates a liquid feed at a design throughput of 10 t per day, with a separation duty corresponding to a removal of 90% of the key component from the stream in which it is recovered. Wetted parts are specified in 316L stainless steel, which is stated here once, and the Materials section works from this statement. The basis of the design is a steady design state, in the sense that the feed composition, the feed condition, and the product duties are the values supplied by the owner for design purposes, and the sizing presented below is a sizing at that state. Operation away from the design state is dealt with in the Risks section, where the open items are collected. It should be noted that product purities beyond the stated duty do not form part of the basis, and no credit has been taken in the sizing for any separation sharper than the duty actually requires.

The feed arrives from upstream storage at its bubble state for the design composition, and the column pressure is set by the condensing medium that is available at the site. The design treats the reboiler and the condenser as integral parts of the column system, with their respective duties following from the internal traffic that the sizing produces. Utility conditions are the site standards for the project, applied exactly as given. The margins contained in the basis are margins on throughput and on the stated duty only; importantly, no hidden margin has been built into the sizing, so that the size produced by this report can be read directly against the duty that it has to meet.

Sizing
The sizing proceeds by means of the standard shortcut route that is commonly used for a binary-style separation, generalised here to the key components named in the basis. A minimum stage count and a minimum reflux are obtained from the equilibrium behaviour of the key pair, and the design stage count and reflux are then set above these minima in line with the usual design practice for columns of this class. The shortcut route has been adopted because the feed is a narrow mixture that is dominated by the key pair; where a wide mixture is being separated, the shortcut values serve as a starting point for a stage-by-stage calculation rather than as a substitute for it.

The diameter follows from the vapour traffic at the tray with the highest loading, checked against flooding using the standard capacity correlations for the tray type that has been selected. Downcomer area, weir loading, and tray spacing are all set by the same practice, and the reboiler and condenser are sized on the duties fixed by the internal traffic. The overall height follows from the stage count, the tray spacing, and the allowances made at the top and bottom for disengagement and sump volume. The pressure drop over the column has been estimated from the tray count and the per-tray drop for the selected tray at the design loading, and the estimate is reported together with the sizing so that the vacuum or pressure duty on the surrounding equipment can be set accordingly. It is worth emphasising that every sizing figure in this section is a shortcut figure; a rating calculation carried out on a selected vendor tray is the step that confirms or revises them, and that step properly belongs to detailed design.

Materials
Wetted parts are manufactured in the grade stated in the Basis. This grade has been selected on account of the corrosive species carried by the feed and the temperatures reached in the reboiler circuit; carbon steel has been excluded from wetted service on corrosion grounds, and the exclusion is recorded here so that a later cost review does not inadvertently reintroduce it. Gaskets and bolting follow the piping class adopted for the column system, with the gasket material checked against the same species list as the shell. Weld procedures for the grade are standard shop procedures, and no special fabrication route is required beyond the normal controls on heat input and interpass temperature that the grade calls for.

External parts, platforms, and supports are carbon steel finished with the project coating system. The condenser and the reboiler follow the column specification on their wetted sides and the utility specification on the water and steam sides. Inspection access has been provided at the sump, at the feed entry, and at the top head, so that the internals whose condition governs the fouling item in the Risks section can be examined without any need to cut the shell.

Risks
Fouling of the internals and of the reboiler remains an open item. The feed carries species that tend to lay down deposits on heated surfaces, and no operating record exists for this mixture at the design conditions, so no fouling rate has been stated and no cleaning interval has been fixed in this report. The risk is managed through inspection access, through space allowed for a spare reboiler bundle, and through a first-year inspection whose findings will be used to set the cleaning practice. The item is not resolved here.

Turndown represents the second open item. The column has been sized at the design throughput, and the minimum rate at which the trays remain loaded and the separation duty still holds has not been established by the shortcut sizing. Operation well below the design rate may call for a smaller tray open area or even for a different internal altogether, and that question is left to the rating step in detailed design. Neither open item changes the basis or the sizing as issued; both are recorded here so that detailed design can take them up in due order.
